principle: 3D objects represent UI; they do not replace the UI.
rules: Every interactive 3D object has a real HTML/UI equivalent.
Keyboard and screen-reader access must remain available without the 3D layer.
Interaction must invoke the existing application feature, not duplicate business logic.
3D animation is cosmetic feedback and may be skipped under reduced motion.
If 3D is unavailable, the HTML UI remains fully functional.
Object state must reflect application state; it must never become a second source of truth.
Focus, hover, click/tap and keyboard behavior must have consistent semantics.
Performance tier is attached to the object, not to the feature correctness.
